Article Title: Jantar Mantar protest: Delhi Metro shuts entry and exit at 12 stations
Article Text:
Interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations.

The metro stations where entry and exit will remain closed are:

Janpath

Patel Chowk

Central Secretariat

Rajiv Chowk

Seva Teerth

Mandi House

Lok Kalyan Marg

INA

Chawri Bazar

Ramakrishna Ashram Marg

New Delhi

Barakhamba

3,000-4,000 people expected at protest

Protesters seek CEC's resignation, impeachment

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Entry and exit at 12 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed until further notice amid heightened security arrangements in New Delhi over a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.However, interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations.These 12 metro stations to remain closed.Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Gandhi Jayanti and deployed additional security personnel in and around New Delhi, officials told news agency PTI.The protest, called by the All India Students' Association (AISA), Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha and Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan, is scheduled to begin at 11 am on Friday.Police sources said around 3,000 to 4,000 people were expected to attend the gathering, prompting heightened security arrangements in the area.Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel have been deployed alongside Delhi Police teams at Jantar Mantar and other key points in New Delhi district.Barricades have been put up, while additional personnel have been positioned at entry and exit points and other sensitive locations to regulate movement and prevent any unauthorised gathering, the sources said.The organisers are seeking the resignation or impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and the conduct of elections.They have also raised concerns over the Election Commission's handling of electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, claiming that it raises questions over the protection of citizens' voting rights.The proposed protest comes amid demonstrations by opposition parties, student groups and civil society activists in Delhi over the functioning of the poll panel and the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: entry and exit at 12 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed until further notice. Interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Gandhi Jayanti.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar protest: AAP's Atishi, AISA's Neha among 700 detained; internet suspended, metro stations shut
Article Text:
Massive protest erupts in two major cities against CEC

Protest planned across cities

CJP's Dipke urges people to join protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park

Police deny permission in Delhi, Mumbai

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Atishi and All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora were detained at Jantar Mantar on Friday as protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls intensified, with the number of people detained crossing 700.Atishi's X post reads, “Modi Ji: We haven't come here to fear your police. To save the right to vote, we will keep fighting ✊🏼”Earlier today, AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj and party MLA Sanjeev Jha were detained by Delhi Police on Friday after they reached Jantar Mantar to join a protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Despite the peaceful protest, Delhi Police arrested MLA Sanjeev Jha ji and Saurabh. But the movement will continue!," reads offical AAP X post.Bharadwaj, on X, later informed that more than 500 people had reached Jantar Mantar ahead of the scheduled protest. "GenZ rocks," he wrote.According to TOI sources, mobile internet services have been disrupted in the Jantar Mantar area, with some users receiving a message stating that internet services have been suspended in the area “as per government instructions” until further notice.READ ALSO: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay plays bus conductor, hands out tickets after expanding free travel scheme Massive protests are planned in Delhi and Mumbai today, with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) set to launch its nationwide agitation from Mumbai’s Shivaji Park.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), All India Students’ Association (AISA), National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) and Indian Youth Congress (IYC) have announced a separate demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.“Appointment of CEC should be transparent; there should be involvement of civil society,” Dipke said in Mumbai.The CJP and opposition parties have criticised Kumar over the SIR of electoral rolls and demanded his resignation.Their criticism intensified after it emerged that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months to certain decisions and orders, some of which they said were issued without their knowledge.The Election Commission later clarified that the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those relating to the SIR, unanimouslyIn a new video, Dipke was seen posing with an auto driver as the two urged commuters and residents to gather at the protest venue. "Chala chala shivaji park.. shivaji park… shivaji park…," the caption reads.The auto driver in the video can be heard saying 'Shivaji Park 4 baje'.Police in both Delhi and Mumbai have denied permission for the proposed protests. In Delhi, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are in force across the New Delhi district, restricting public meetings or assemblies of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas without prior written permission.Delhi DCP said that the restrictions have been imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement.In Mumbai, police have also denied permission for the proposed gathering at Shivaji Park. Police said they were not authorised to permit such a gathering there in view of a 2013 Bombay High Court order and described the area as a silence zone.Meanwhile, the Delhi Metro has also closed entry and exit at 11 stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Janpath, Patel Chowk, Seva Teerth, Mandi House, Lok Kalyan Marg, INA, Chawri Bazar, Ramakrishna Ashram Marg and New Delhi, until further notice.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Atishi and All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora were detained at Jantar Mantar on Friday. The number of people detained crossing 700 as protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls intensified. In Delhi, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita are in force.

Article Title: Karnataka BJP leader booked over alleged bid to delete names of 198 'Muslim voters'
Article Text:
BLO lodges FIR against BJP leader over alleged bid to delete 198 voter names during SIR

NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against Karnataka BJP leader Ravi Patil and others for allegedly attempting to get the names of 198 Muslim voters deleted from the electoral roll in Belagavi district through Form-7 applications during the ongoing SIR process, police said on Friday, as cited by news agency PTI.Police said the case was registered at Belagavi Market police station on September 30 based on a complaint by Meerasab Sanadi, a Booth Level Agent for Ward No. 12 in the Belagavi North Assembly constituency.At least two FIRs have so far been registered over alleged “SIR irregularities”, including one in Mysuru against local BJP leaders and others, with the complainant alleging a “conspiracy” to get his, his family's and other members of the “Muslim community's votes deleted during the SIR process and thereby, hurting the religious sentiments of the community and creating disturbance in society”.The FIR has been registered under Sections 318(4) (cheating), 336(3) (forgery), 336(4) (forgery intended to harm reputation), 353 (statements conducing to public mischief), 61(2) (criminal conspiracy), 3(5) (common intention), 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause a riot) and 190 (liability of members of an unlawful assembly for offences committed in pursuit of its common object) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police said further investigation is underway.According to the FIR, the complainant said he was assisting the Booth Level Officer (BLO) in the Election Commission’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and helping verify voter details.He alleged that on September 22, around 2.30 pm, the accused, including Patil, Shankar Beerappa Naik and Pashant Deepak Mundinmani, along with 20 to 25 others, allegedly assembled with the intention of targeting voters and conspired to have their names removed from the electoral roll.The accused allegedly prepared forged documents and submitted them to the BLO, falsely claiming that they were genuine documents issued by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), the complainant alleged. He further alleged that the Form-7 applications submitted with the purportedly fake documents included the names of 198 voters, including him and his family members."They allegedly exerted pressure on the BLO and made another person speak over the phone claiming to be the ERO and obtained his signature, thereby cheating the complainant and the voters," the FIR said.Form 7 is the prescribed application form for filing an objection to the proposed inclusion or deletion of a name from the existing electoral roll.In another such case in Bidar, 40-year-old businessman and Bhalki voter Mohammed Ateeq Ahmed alleged in his complaint that 3,244 voters, including him, were falsely shown as “shifted/absent” through Form 7 applications during the SIR of electoral rolls.According to the FIR, Ahmed alleged that the applications were submitted without obtaining authenticated documents from the affected voters and that their signatures were forged with the intention of getting their names deleted from the electoral roll.Following his complaint, police registered an FIR on October 1, naming 32 people as accused in connection with the alleged irregularities.Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar, along with his Cabinet colleagues and MLAs, staged a sit-in outside the office of Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar on Thursday, demanding registration of an FIR over alleged “electoral fraud” during the ongoing SIR of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: FIR has been registered against Karnataka BJP leader Ravi Patil and others for allegedly attempting to get the names of 198 Muslim voters deleted from the electoral roll. The case was registered at Belagavi Market police station on September 30 based on a complaint by Meerasab Sanadi.

Article Title: 'We would work under you': Adhir invites Mamata to rejoin Congress, but with a rider
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A day after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Thursday asked TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee to rejoin the Congress along with her remaining MLAs and MPs. However, the invitation came with a condition of “leaving behind her baggage”, an apparent reference to her nephew and TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee.A day after Mamata attended the INDIA bloc meeting in Delhi, Chowdhury said, “There is no need for any separate entity at this moment. Not much is left of the TMC after its defeat in the assembly elections.”“We would urge Mamata Banerjee to join the Congress along with all the leftover MLAs and MPs. I will also make this appeal to the Congress high command that let her rejoin the party. We would accept her leadership in Bengal and work with her,” he added.Chowdhury also urged the Congress high command to facilitate the merger and said that Mamata should, as a gesture of cooperation similar to the October 6 Nandigram assembly bypoll, extend support to the Congress candidate in Rejinagar.“As a friendly gesture, just as she has supported the Congress candidate in Nandigram, she should also extend support to the Congress candidate in Rejinagar,” he said.“As she has taken shelter in the Congress-led INDIA alliance, she should join the party.In Bengal, we would work under you in Congress,” he added.This comes a day after Mamata Banerjee, following the INDIA bloc meeting in Delhi, asserted that the opposition alliance was “very much united” as she sought to project a united opposition front while demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The developments come as the TMC faces one of its deepest organisational crises since its formation following the West Bengal assembly election results, with separate rebellions emerging in its legislative and parliamentary wings.Within weeks of the election verdict, the TMC legislature party split, with 58 rebel MLAs backing expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their leader of the opposition. The assembly speaker subsequently recognised the rival bloc.The rebellion was followed by a parallel churn in the TMC’s parliamentary wing, with rebel MPs also challenging Mamata Banerjee’s leadership.TMC MP Sougata Roy, however, said the party would consider any such proposal only if it came formally from the Congress leadership.“He (Chowdhury) has said what he felt. We have nothing to say. TMC is a separate party now. If Congress wants to come with an official proposal, we will discuss the matter in the party. The TMC is very much part of the INDIA bloc,” Roy said.Asked about Chowdhury’s “baggage” remark, Roy said no decision concerning the party could be taken without Abhishek Banerjee.“He is our leader and national general secretary,” Roy said.Mamata had broken away from the Congress in 1998 to establish the Trinamool Congress, which subsequently built its political identity by challenging both the Congress and the Left Front.
Article Summary: Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Thursday asked TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee to rejoin the Congress along with her remaining MLAs and MPs. However, the invitation came with a condition of “leaving behind her baggage’, an apparent reference to her nephew and TMC national general secretary AbhishekBanerjee. The developments come as the TMC faces one of its deepest organisational crises since its formation following the West Bengal election results.

Article Title: BJP slams Congress, accuses Rahul of hypocrisy, lying

Article Title: ‘15,000 voters targeted’: Rahul Gandhi’s fresh attack on EC over Karnataka rolls
Article Text:
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday launched a scathing attack on the Election Commission and accused it of erasing nearly 15,000 voters from electoral rolls in Karnataka’s Belagavi region.In a social media post on X, Rahul said that a massive “flood” of Form 7 applications was filed in bulk over three days to remove targeted groups from the voter list.“In just three days - September 22, 23, and 24 - there was a flood of Form 7 applications to remove nearly 15,000 voters... Muslims, SCs, STs, and OBCs are being systematically targeted because they do not vote for the BJP,” Rahul said.“I had already exposed this method of vote theft - votes are deleted through software in a centralised manner. ‘Select’ people are targeted as BJP and EC officials collude to fill out Form 7 in bulk through automated means - and in the blink of an eye, millions vanish from the voter list. And all of this is controlled from the top,” he added.The Congress leader also demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar immediately take action or step down, alleging that refusal to register an FIR undermines democratic institutions.“Karnataka Congress leaders are at this moment demanding an FIR against the culprits at the Karnataka CEO’s office. Why is the CEO refusing this FIR? In this way, Modi, Shah, and Gyanesh are collectively destroying democracy through SIR. This is treason. That's why I'm saying Gyanesh Kumar should resign and become an approver, and there should be an investigation against Modi and Shah,” he added.Form 7 is the official document prescribed by the Election Commission for objecting to the inclusion of or seeking the deletion of a name from an existing electoral roll.In Belagavi, local election officials reportedly received thousands of such applications over a span of 72 hours, triggering alarm among local Congress workers and booth-level officers (BLOs).Meanwhile, the poll panel and regional authorities clarified the procedural safeguards surrounding Form 7 filings. Election officials stressed that no voter’s name can be deleted automatically or solely based on the submission of a Form 7.Every application requires physical field verification, notices to be issued to the affected voter, and due process to be conducted by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) before any deletion is finalised, the panel said.Election officials instructed local BLOs to halt the immediate processing of suspected bulk filings and initiated internal inquiries to trace the origin of the submissions and verify whether the signatures were genuine.Earlier on Wednesday, INDIA bloc leaders held a coordination meeting in New Delhi and announced a series of protests against the EC.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said Opposition parties would organise a nationwide “Save Democracy March” at the district level from October 2 to October 8.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi launched a scathing attack on the Election Commission. He accused it of erasing nearly 15,000 voters from electoral rolls in Karnataka’s Belagavi region. Rahul said that a massive ‘flood’ of Form 7 applications was filed in bulk over three days.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note
Article Text:
BJP CMs Rekha Gupta, Devendra Fadnavis and Yogi Adityanath

What BJP CMs said

Rahul Gandhi’s cryptic post

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The controversy

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.
Article Summary: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday. The chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions” In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: Section 163 BNSS in force in New Delhi ahead of protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
Article Text:
Security has also been tightened in the national capital ahead of the proposed protest.

Section 163 BNSS order in force in New Delhi

Atishi urges people to reach Jantar Mantar at 10 am

Traffic restrictions

, diversions around Jantar Mantar





NEW DELHI: A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, is in force in New Delhi district ahead of a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Friday.The order has been imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement. Security has also been tightened in the national capital ahead of the proposed protest.Under the prohibitory order, public meetings or assemblies of five or more persons, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas are prohibited without prior written permission.Shouting slogans or making speeches is also prohibited without prior written permission. The order further prohibits carrying firearms, banners, placards, lathis, swords, sticks, brickbats or similar articles.Citizens, visitors and all stakeholders have been advised to strictly comply with the order and refrain from any unauthorised gathering or prohibited activity.Violation of the order shall invite legal action under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and other applicable provisions of law.Earlier, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA and former Delhi chief minister Atishi on Thursday appealed to people to reach Jantar Mantar at 10 am on Friday, amid a proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the functioning of the Election Commission and its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Atishi also posted on X, "Let's go to Jantar Mantar 2 October 2026 10 AM."In a video message, Atishi said, "When India became independent in 1947, the most important right we received was the right to vote. We could choose whose government would be formed, and we could choose our own representatives. But today, the BJP is trying to snatch that right away from us through Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. If the right to vote is in danger, it means our democracy is in danger. Therefore, I appeal to all of you to reach Jantar Mantar tomorrow, October 2nd, at 10:00 AM to protect your right to vote. " Delhi Traffic Police has also issued a traffic advisory for October 2, warning commuters of restrictions and regulated movement around Jantar Mantar and adjoining areas.Traffic diversions and regulations will be in place around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, GPO, Tolstoy Marg, Jantar Mantar Road, Parliament Street and adjoining roads.Traffic from Connaught Place towards Patel Chowk will be diverted through alternate routes as directed by traffic personnel, while movement from Patel Chowk towards GPO will be regulated or diverted at appropriate points.Traffic movement on Tolstoy Marg will also be regulated or diverted, with commuters advised to avoid the stretch wherever possible. Movement on Jantar Mantar Road will be restricted or diverted, and motorists have been advised to use alternate routes.The traffic police has advised the public to avoid Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street, Ashoka Road and adjoining roads wherever possible.
Article Summary: A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, is in force in New Delhi district. The order has been imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA and former Delhi chief minister Atishi appealed to people to reach Jantar Mantar at 10 am on Friday.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Couple booked for duping three of ₹8L in crypto scam
Article Text:
Pune:





Hinjewadi police on Wednesday registered a case against a couple for allegedly duping three people of Rs 8.15 lakh on the promise of giving them high returns on cryptocurrency investments. A 23-year-old woman from Wakad, who works with a private company, lodged a police complaint on Wednesday.An officer said the complainant came into contact with the couple in April, when they allegedly promised her good returns if she invested in cryptocurrency through them.Over two months, she invested Rs 2.73 lakh, and got a father-son duo she knew to also invest Rs 5.42 lakh through the suspects.“After waiting for almost four months, when she did not receive returns or even her money back, she approached the police,” the officer said.The police have registered a case under BNS section 318 (cheating) and relevant sections of the Information Technology Act.
Article Summary: A 23-year-old woman from Wakad, who works with a private company, lodged a police complaint. A father-son duo she knew also invested Rs 5.42 lakh through the suspects. The police have registered a case under BNS section 318 (cheating) and relevant sections of the Information Technology Act.

Article Title: Sharad Pawar to visit drought-affected tehsils from Friday
Article Text:
Sharad Pawar will interact with the farmers in Baramati on Friday morning. He will also visit Purandar tehsil to review the impact of drought on farms

Pune





: Former Union agriculture minister Sharad Pawar will undertake a tour of the state’s drought-affected areas starting from his hometown, Baramati, on Friday.NCP(SP) functionaries said Pawar will interact with the farmers in Baramati on Friday morning. He will also visit Purandar tehsil to review the impact of drought on farms.Pawar has written two letters to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , suggesting various measures for the state govt to provide relief to distressed farmers. He has also urged the chief minister to convene a three-day special assembly session to discuss the drought situation and subsequent relief measures. The former Union minister has demanded that the state govt provide Rs1 lakh per hectare in assistance to the affected farmers.
Article Summary: Sharad Pawar will interact with the farmers in Baramati on Friday morning. He will also visit Purandar tehsil to review the impact of drought on farms. The former Union minister has demanded that the state govt provide Rs1 lakh per hectare in assistance to the affected farmers.

Article Title: Astrologer Ashok Kharat in Nashik police custody in cheating case
Article Text:
Nashik

:





Astrologer Ashok Kharat allegedly posed as a divine incarnation and promised “divine powers” and business prosperity to dupe a cloth merchant of Rs 2.6 lakh and three gold rings weighing 20gm. A city court on Wednesday remanded Kharat to police custody till Oct 2 in the cheating and Black Magic Act case registered with the Sarkarwada police on March 28.Police said Kharat convinced the merchant that gemstones provided by him would bring prosperity and divine powers. The merchant allegedly handed him three gold rings and Rs 2.6 lakh in instalments.In return, Kharat allegedly gave him fake yellow-metal rings fitted with imitation stones worth barely Rs 5,000.The alleged fraud took place in Dec 2022. The merchant, however, approached police only in March after media reports about cases of sexual assault and black magic registered against Kharat came out.Kharat has been behind bars since March 18. He faces 18 cases in Nashik and Ahilyanagar, including eight related to sexual assault. He also faces cases of cheating and one involving alleged extortion and provisions of the Black Magic Act.State govt has constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe 11 cases against Kharat. The Sarkarwada cheating case is being investigated separately.“We have received Kharat’s custody till Oct 2. Sarkarwada police will also investigate one more case against him,” investigating officer, assistant inspector Prakash Patil, said.
Article Summary: Astrologer Ashok Kharat allegedly posed as a divine incarnation and promised ‘divine powers’ and business prosperity to dupe a cloth merchant. Kharat has been behind bars since March 18. He faces 18 cases in Nashik and Ahilyanagar, including eight related to sexual assault. He also faces cases of cheating and one involving alleged extortion.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Boy riding motorcycle, father booked for causing road accident in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police have registered a case against a 14-year-old boy and his father after a motorcycle ridden by the minor collided with a scooter at Gandhipuram here.According to police, the accident occurred on the 100 Feet Road around 5.35pm on Sept 22. The boy, with his father Vikram sitting on the pillion seat, was riding a motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner. The motorcycle collided with a scooter ridden by Sivakumar, 54, of Manjeshwari Colony near Kovilmedu.Due to the impact, Sivakumar fell on the road and suffered injuries on his right ankle and left elbow. He was taken to a private hospital for treatment. After treatment, Sivakumar lodged a complaint with the traffic investigation wing (east) on Tuesday.Police registered a case under sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 181(4) of the Motor Vehicles Act.Police have issued a stern warning to all parents not to allow minors without driving licences to drive vehicles.
Article Summary: Coimbatore city police have registered a case against a 14-year-old boy and his father. A motorcycle ridden by the minor collided with a scooter at Gandhipuram. The boy, with his father Vikram sitting on the pillion seat, was riding a motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.

Article Title: CM Vijay’s visit: Traffic diversions announced in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police have announced temporary traffic diversions on arterial roads in view of the visit of chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday. The CM will arrive here en route to Dharapuram, where he will be campaigning for P Sathyabama who is the TVK candidate for the Oct 6 byelection.Buses entering Coimbatore city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road. Instead, these vehicles must divert at Neelambur and take L&T Bypass via Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to enter the city. Light vehicles from the Neelambur side are also advised to go via L&T Bypass, Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to reach the city.Vehicles exiting the city via the Avinashi Road must make a U-turn at Lakshmi Mills Junction and proceed via Puliyakulam, Ramanathapuram and Singanallur to reach L&T Bypass.Light motor vehicles exiting via the Avinashi Road and the V K Road should take a diversion through the Masakalipalayam Road to reach Singanallur. Vehicles arriving via Avinashi Road / Hope College Junction must make a U-turn at Tidel Park Junction and proceed via the Kamarajar Road to Singanallur.Heavy vehicles heading towards the Avinashi Road from Kalapatti Junction must divert at Kalapatti Junction and proceed via Thennampalayam.Heavy vehicles approaching the Avinashi Road from the Goldwins Road should turn right at the Housing Unit Road / Maruti Bakery Junction and proceed via the Veeriyampalayam Road to reach Kalapatti Junction.Passengers are advised to reach the airport at least 30 minutes prior to their scheduled travel time. Parking for call taxis and private vehicles on the airport premises will not be permitted.Entry of trucks into the city is prohibited between 7am and 9pm on Wednesday.Trucks travelling from Walayar towards Salem on the Kochi - Salem National Highway are advised to take the alternative route via Palathurai Junction and Karpagam College Junction towards Othakkalmandapam, Chettipalayam, Pappampatti, Selakarichal and Karadivavi. Trucks going towards Walayar are advised to travel to Sulur via Chinthamanipudur and Pappampatti. Trucks travelling from Annur towards Avinashi and Karumathampatti are prohibited from passing through Somanur.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay will arrive in Coimbatore on Wednesday. Buses entering city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road.

Article Title: Stolen 15th-century idol seized in Madurai; 3 arrested
Article Text:
CID seized a 15th-century Thirugnanasambandar metal idol, valued at about 1 crore,

Madurai

:





The Tamil Nadu Idol Wing CID seized a 15th-century Thirugnanasambandar metal idol, valued at about ₹1 crore, from a car in Madurai and arrested three men.Acting on specific information, a team kept surveillance near Yettayapuram Thoppu at the Madurai-Tirumangalam four-way junction on Sept 29. Police intercepted an Innova around 1.55 pm and recovered the standing idol along with its pedestal. It measured about three feet and weighed 52.180 kg. Idol Wing officials identified it as a representation of Thirugnanasambandar from the Vijayanagara period.The arrested men were identified as Jeyavelan, 48, Pandiyarajan, 37, and Akbar, 52, all residents of Madurai. Based on a report submitted by Sub-Inspector R Ramasamy, the Idol Wing CID registered a case on Sept 30 under relevant provisions of the BNSS and BNS.The accused, the idol and the vehicle were produced before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate in Madurai, who remanded the three men in judicial custody until Oct 13.Inspector D Jeyakumar has been appointed investigating officer. Police are probing the idol’s origin, trying to identify the temple from which it was allegedly stolen and tracing others suspected to be part of the trafficking network.
Article Summary: The Tamil Nadu Idol Wing CID seized a 15th-century Thirugnanasambandar metal idol, valued at about ₹1 crore, from a car in Madurai and arrested three men. The arrested men were identified as Jeyavelan, 48, Pandiyarajan, 37, and Akbar, 52, all residents of Madurai.

Article Title: DMK man held in Srirangam temple land fraud
Article Text:
DMK Srirangam area secretary M Ramkumar was arrested on Thursday by Trichy city crime branch police





Trichy/Madurai: Hours after his anticipatory bail plea was dismissed by the Madurai bench of Madras high court DMK Srirangam area secretary M Ramkumar was arrested on Thursday by Trichy city crime branch police on charges of illegally grabbing a parcel of land -- worth Rs 50 crore -- belonging to Srirangam temple.The FIR in connection with the case was registered on Sept 13 based on a complaint by Srirangam temple JC S Sivaramakumar. Police booked M Ramkumar of Thiruvanaikoil who is the Srirangam DMK area secretary, Padma Rengarajan of Chennai, Vijaya Krishnasamy of Bengaluru, R Soundararajan of Chennai, R Venkata Varadhan, and former Srirangam sub-registrar Vanitha under six sections related to cheating, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.According to the FIR, the 7,515 sq ft parcel of land “illegally grabbed” in 2022 by the accused forms part of a larger 5.87acre property belonging to Srirangam temple. A DMK office was built on the parcel of land illegally grabbed.After the case was registered by police, Ramkumar moved court to seek anticipatory bail. The Madurai bench of Madras HC dismissed the plea on Thursday, leading to his arrest by the police. Anticipatory bail petition of then sub registrar Vanitha also was dismissed by the court.However, Ramkumar’s wife, Andal, said he was arrested on Thursday morning while he was going to Madurai for the court hearing. “He has been arrested on false charges,” she told reporters.
Article Summary: DMK Srirangam area secretary M Ramkumar was arrested on Thursday by Trichy city crime branch police. He was accused of illegally grabbing a parcel of land -- worth Rs 50 crore -- belonging to Srirangsam temple. His anticipatory bail plea was dismissed by the Madurai bench of Madras high court.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Police file case against college based on PhD scholar’s complaint
Article Text:
Kochi:





Aluva West Police have registered an FIR against Sree Narayana Guru College, Coimbatore, and its department head following allegations of cheating.The FIR was registered on Saturday based on a complaint filed by PhD scholar Sachu Muraleedharan. He filed a private complaint before the judicial first-class magistrate court, Aluva, which forwarded the complaint to the police for appropriate action.Professor and head of the department of social work Maria Yesuraja has also been named in the FIR. The complaint is that Muraleedharan was allegedly cheated of Rs 26,000 after being promised that his research paper would be published in Kanpur Philosophers Journal, a journal included in UGC-CARE List. The complainant alleged that he later discovered that his article was not published in the genuine Kanpur Philosophers Journal but in a clone journal, the FIR says.
Article Summary: Sree Narayana Guru College, Coimbatore, and its department head have been named in the FIR. The complaint is that Sachu Muraleedharan was allegedly cheated of Rs 26,000 after being promised that his research paper would be published in a journal included in UGC-CARE List.

Article Title: Rash driving case: Kerala HC stays trial against IAS officer Sreeram Venkitaraman
Article Text:
Sreeram Venkitaraman

Kochi

:





The high court has stayed the trial in the 2019 road accident case involving IAS officer Sreeram Venkitaraman on a petition filed by the widow of journalist K M Basheer, the accident victim.Justice G Girish issued the interim order on a petition filed by Basheer’s widow Jaseela C, challenging a govt order dated Sept 17 rejecting her representation seeking the appointment of a special public prosecutor for the trial. According to her, the order was contrary to the submission made before the court in an earlier litigation. The court adjourned the petition to Oct 27 for the state govt to obtain instructions.Previously, the court had disposed of Jaseela’s plea seeking the appointment of a special prosecutor, based on the state govt’s submission that a decision had been taken to appoint A Santhosh Kumar but that a formal notification had not yet been issued. While disposing of the petition, the court had also directed the additional sessions court – 4, Thiruvananthapuram , to defer the trial proceedings for a month, enabling the state to appoint the special public prosecutor.However, a govt order issued by the additional chief secretary, home, rejected Jaseela’s representation. The order stated that although the public prosecutor had submitted before the HC that the govt had, in principle, decided to appoint Santhosh Kumar as special public prosecutor, no such decision or instruction had been issued by the govt. The order also stated that no shortcoming, weakness, incompetence or inefficiency on the part of the present public prosecutor had been pointed out.Accordingly, Jaseela approached the court challenging the home department’s order, alleging that it was contrary to the assurance given by the state govt before the court. Basheer, the Thiruvananthapuram bureau chief of a Malayalam daily, was killed on Aug 3, 2019, after his motorcycle was hit by a car allegedly driven by Venkitaraman.
Article Summary: The high court has stayed the trial in the 2019 road accident case involving IAS officer Sreeram Venkitaraman. Justice G Girish issued the interim order on a petition filed by Basheer’s widow Jaseela C. The court adjourned the petition to Oct 27 for the state govt to obtain instructions.

Article Title: Defamatory remarks about CM: Anto Augustine moves Kerala HC to quash case
Article Text:
Reporter TV managing director Anto Augustine

Kochi:





Reporter TV managing director Anto Augustine has approached the high court seeking to quash a criminal case registered against him over alleged defamatory remarks about chief minister V D Satheesan.The case arose from a complaint alleging that Augustine had conspired with other accused and forged documents purporting to show that the chief minister had solemnised another marriage while his first marriage was still subsisting. A case was registered at the cyber police station in Thiruvananthapuram on a complaint filed by Raju P Nair of Ernakulam. It was later transferred to the Kalamassery police station on the assumption that the alleged place of occurrence fell within its territorial jurisdiction.According to the petition, cognisance of the offence of defamation is barred except on a complaint filed by the person aggrieved, in terms of Section 222(1) of the BNSS. In this case, the complainant is a third party and not a “person aggrieved” within the meaning of the provision. Augustine further claimed that there was no allegation that he had made any false document or record or used any such document as genuine.Augustine stated that while addressing a seminar on media ethics at Pathanamthitta, he had said that two individuals had approached him claiming to have news worth Rs 1 crore concerning the CM’s alleged second marriage. They had also shown him documents relating to the claim. However, verification revealed that the news was fake. According to Augustine, the case was registered against him after he himself disclosed the incident in a speech, and the registration of the case was legally unsustainable.
Article Summary: Reporter TV managing director Anto Augustine has approached the high court seeking to quash a criminal case. The case arose from a complaint alleging that Augustine had conspired with other accused and forged documents purporting to show that the chief minister had solemnised another marriage while his first marriage was still subsisting. According to Augustine, the case was registered against him after he himself disclosed the incident in a speech.
